description: Map an area or a network as a whole: the grid's cells, a wall face, a network's members, feed paths. Read only.

options.box: area: Two corners; at most 20000 2 m cells. network: Box form: the pieces in it (alone: open ends in it).
options.network: area: Only pieces on these networks. network, feeds: A network: its id, a piece or device on it, or {id, port}.
options.prefab: area: Prefab: a whole name, a hash, or parts with * ('*Battery*', '*Tank*Insulated*': each part, any order); or a list of them. network: Only members whose prefab holds this part.
options.cell_detail: occupancy: cells {at, empty, frame_id, faces, small}; full: cells {at, room_id, frame, walls, small, support} in place of those. Default occupancy.
options.half_width: Half-width of the map in metres. Default 4.
options.free_rects: {w, h, one_section, require_wall, limit}: where a w x h rectangle fits.
options.near: Centre: [x, y, z], "player", "looking_at" or a thing's id (its position); with radius.
options.id: The root device (an APC output, a generator). Any what that takes an id takes a list: one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, payload | error}], count, success_count, error_count}, payload the one-id reply; a bad id is a row with error.

area.summary: the 2 m cells of a box or room: what occupies each, the pieces, devices, ports and networks

box.description: Two corners; at most 20000 2 m cells.

networks.description: Include the networks of the pieces.

include.description: refund: each piece's removal refund; piece_cells: every small cell of a long piece.

cell_detail.description: occupancy: cells {at, empty, frame_id, faces, small}; full: cells {at, room_id, frame, walls, small, support} in place of those.

limit.x-script: The first n in order (2 m cells); left out, every one.

text: A big area is many pages (125 cells at most each), and output_file writes one page. For a whole area, page with offset (has_more) or use a smaller box per call.
x-script-text: A big area is many pages (125 cells each); r['cells'].walk() goes through them all.
